incoming.explanation: The elimination scaffold has no content unless there is a profile to test candidates against.
The candidate-landscape outcome is the result of applying the matching-criteria profile.

outgoing.explanation: The 1638-early-1641 arrival window bounds the 'gone from English records by c.1641' strand of the profile.
The occupation finding (a tailor by trade) is one strand of the shared matching-criteria profile.
The first-wife-Mary finding is one strand of the shared matching-criteria profile.
The reconstructed five-child roster is one strand of the shared matching-criteria profile.
The c.1602-1610 birth-window finding is one strand of the shared matching-criteria profile.

finding.shortLabel: Shared matching-criteria profile: tailor, wife Mary, three English-born children, birth c.1602–1608, gone from England by 1641
finding.statement: Any English candidate for the Braintree emigrant must satisfy one shared profile drawn from his colonial baseline: a tailor by trade; married to a wife named Mary; father in England of Mary, Richard and John Jr., with Sarah possible; born in England about 1602-1608, read off his own 1652/3 age deposition; and gone from the English record by the time he first appears in Massachusetts in June 1641. Peter and Isaac are excluded from the English child test — neither has a baptism anywhere in Britain and both were almost certainly born in New England — so a candidate household is tested against three named English children rather than five. A settled Puritan household is a soft fifth criterion. This whole profile, not a bare surname match, is the shared test applied to every alternative candidate.
